title: Paper v2 portfolio can show RUNNING while no tickable live session exists
description:
After restarting production services, Paper v2 scheduler is healthy but has no tickable sessions. The portfolio live_loop1_tdx_20260514_precreated remains portfolio status RUNNING, while its latest live session is terminal FAILED. The running-summary endpoint still returns a large running summary payload, which can mislead operators into thinking live simulation is active.

Impact: operators may start the scheduler and assume the live portfolio is running, while scheduler run_once has session_count=0 and cannot process anything. The UI/API needs an explicit 'RUNNING portfolio without operable session' state and remediation guidance.
reproduce_command: Call /api/v1/paper-v2/session-scheduler/status and query paper_v2.trade_session tickable statuses after production restart: scheduler is healthy but tickable session count is 0 while portfolio paper_8f9b5368e86344ba8d699b4995ae665e status is RUNNING and latest session is FAILED.
required_verification: API exposes an explicit no_operable_session or equivalent health flag for RUNNING/READY portfolios whose latest session is terminal.
UI clearly displays that scheduler has no tickable session and gives non-trading-window remediation guidance.
Regression/E2E test covers portfolio RUNNING plus latest session FAILED plus scheduler session_count=0.
closure_requirements: Operators cannot confuse a RUNNING portfolio shell with an actively scheduled live session.
Scheduler status/run-once response and running page agree on tickable session count.
No automatic session creation occurs during the 09:15-15:00 blocked state-change window.
non_goals: Do not auto-create or switch sessions during trading hours.
Do not hide failed sessions from the operator.
Do not change portfolio lifecycle semantics without a separate design decision.

events.note: Created from production Paper v2 live-session diagnostic after 2026-05-14 live simulation failure.
Verified locally in commit 1ce3bef with targeted backend tests.
